description.narrative: The project is implemented in Zimbabwe. The main outcome areas it contributes to is opposing the backlash increasing gender equality. The main rights holders are women with leadership positions in the wings/assemblies of the political parties represented in Parliament, top leadership/structures of political parties represented in Parliament, selected women Councillors, marginalised and poor women living in target constituencies and Wards led by women Members of Parliament and Councillors- Ward Consultative Forum/Constituency Consultative Forum, selected Parliament of Zimbabwe Portfolio Committees, Provincial Councils, targeted local authorities- chiefs, headmen, local leaders, and officials and selected like-minded civil society organisations including the faith based institutions and labour unions.Through focusing on the structures and norms in varies spheres of the political space the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas. This will be done by capacity building to rights holders, but also to engage constructively with the institutions and the individual political parties in a non-biased and informed way.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Women in Politics Support Unit and The Palme Center.WiPSU was formed in April 2001 by women for women to operate as a feminist resources base to support women s political participation. Initially it was termed Women in Parliament Support Unit however within six months it undertook a name review to Women in Politics Support Unit to represent the broad spectrum of women political participation.WiPSU works with women in communities, women in local government (elected councillors) and Local Government, women in parliament and Parliament of Zimbabwe, as well as women in political parties.Other Donors to the OrganisationOrganisation is Donor Financed.Supporters are the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Netherlands Embassy, Womankind, Diakonia and Hivos.Diakonia is also part of the Zimbabwe Europe Network and there are are networking and coordination efforts being carried out in that capacity.It is mostly reflected on operational level, when travels or advocacy work are being carried out.Project ObjectiveThe aim of the project is to create an enabling political and socio-cultural environment that facilitates women s equal representation in public political office.The specific objectives are,1. Political Parties demonstrate increased political will and commitment to implement internal party quotas and fully operationalize laws and policies that promote equal representation in political party processes and systems.2. Traditional Leaders, publicly support improved positive public perception of women as political leaders Chiefs and headmen lead in.3. Women in Leadership (Political Parliamentary, Provincial, Local Government and Communities) demonstrate enhanced capacity including knowledge, skills and confidence has been.
